issuing_body: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
title: Transcribed Interview of Tony Lourey

interview_status.truthfulness_warning: Committee staff stated that although Lourey would not be sworn, federal law required truthful answers to Congress and congressional staff and knowingly false statements could be criminally prosecuted.

supports: Lourey testified that during his 2019 tenure as DHS commissioner he communicated with then-chief of staff Christopher Schmitter about program-integrity concerns and the oversight tools and authority DHS needed for medication-assisted therapy, nonemergency medical transportation, and Child Care Assistance Program issues.
Lourey said he could not speak to conversations he was not involved in and therefore could not say whether Schmitter passed those concerns to Governor Walz.

When explicitly asked to speculate whether program-integrity concerns at that level likely would have been brought to the Governor's attention, Lourey said it was likely. That response is speculation, not personal-knowledge testimony.

Lourey testified that he did not recall resistance from Governor's-office staff to raising fraud/program-integrity concerns and did not know of Governor's-office staff who pushed back on efforts to strengthen anti-fraud tools.
Lourey denied that Walz or Ellison directed him to ignore fraud and said he had no reason to believe either knowingly ignored fraud in DHS-administered programs.
Lourey testified that his resignation from DHS was unrelated to fraud or the Walz administration's handling of fraud.
selected_locators: PDF pp.13-16, extracted lines 316-390: fraud/program-integrity discussions and no recalled pushback
PDF pp.39-40, extracted lines 971-996: 2019 Schmitter communications and explicit speculation about Governor notice
PDF pp.90-92, extracted lines 2200-2233: resignation unrelated to fraud
PDF pp.96-97, extracted lines 2348-2361: denials of direction to ignore fraud
important_qualifications: This interview was not sworn; it is classified TRANSCRIBED_INTERVIEW because the Committee expressly imposed a legal duty of truthful response and warned of false-statement prosecution.

Lourey's statement that Governor notice was 'likely' was given only after the questioner expressly asked him to speculate. It must not be presented as a statement of personal knowledge that Walz was briefed.
The interview does establish 2019 program-integrity communications between Lourey and Schmitter at the Governor's-office level, but it does not close the notice chain from Schmitter to Walz.
